findings.title: Regex does not match STATUS.md bold-marker format — plan-doc worked Example 1 (✅ STATUS.md format) fails the regex; check-invocation-log-entry.sh would reject all legitimately-formatted TF rows for the onboarded-operator-bump path; enforcement spec is incomplete for this path
findings.evidence:
The R6 file-agnostic fix correctly removed the leading `^- \*\*` anchor from the pre-R6 regex so that the regex could match both STATUS.md and DISPATCH-NOTE formats. However, the pre-R6 regex also contained `\*\*` AFTER the adopter slug as the closing bold marker (i.e. `...jrnb2024-pim\*\* \((open|...)\):`). The R6 fix dropped this trailing `\*\*` from the pattern while retaining the slug character class `[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+`. The resulting regex expects the adopter slug to be immediately followed by ` \(` (space then open-paren). In STATUS.md bold format, the slug is followed by `**` (two asterisk closing bold markers) before ` (`. The regex engine therefore: finds slug='jrnb2024-pim', expects ' (', finds '** (' — NO MATCH.

Verification:
- Plan-doc Example 1 (line 58): `✅ - **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open): Renovate disabled on PIM; operator-bumped @abc123 at 024C; track until adopter enables Renovate cohort.`
- Python 3: `re.search(r'TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+ \((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\): \S.{19,}', '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open): Renovate disabled on PIM; ...')` returns `None`.
- The plan-doc states (line 55): 'The regex is **file-agnostic**: it matches the TF reference content, not the surrounding markdown (so the same line passes whether it has a `- **...**` STATUS.md bullet wrapper...)'. This claim is false: the regex fails on STATUS.md bullet wrapper format.

Completeness governance dimension: The spec's acceptance criterion at §6 024B requires `check-invocation-log-entry.sh` to cover all four CI behaviors including `onboarded-operator-bump: requires log entry + target match + TF-024X-renovate-<adopter-slug> STATUS.md row matching invariant 2's regex format spec literally`. If the regex literally fails on STATUS.md bold format, the 024B acceptance criterion CANNOT be met without deviating from the regex literal. An executor implementing the regex literally satisfies the wording of §6 024B but produces a check that breaks the onboarded-operator-bump enforcement path: every legitimately-formatted TF row in STATUS.md (`- **TF-024X-renovate-<adopter-slug>** (status): description`) would always fail CI, blocking legitimate onboarded-operator-bump slices. This is a completeness defect because the plan-doc's enforcement specification is demonstrably incomplete: it specifies a regex that cannot enforce what it claims to enforce for the STATUS.md path.

Secondary consequence: Examples 3–6 (the four negative STATUS.md examples) also fail the regex, but for the wrong reason (the `**` breaks the match, not the specific description defects they are intended to illustrate). This means the examples do not actually validate the \S.{19,} enforcement for the STATUS.md path.
findings.recommendation:
Add an optional non-capturing group for the closing bold marker in the slug segment. Change the regex from:

```
TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+ \((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\): \S.{19,}
```

to:

```
TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+(?:\*\*)? \((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\): \S.{19,}
```

The `(?:\*\*)?` group is optional (zero or one occurrence). It matches the closing bold marker `**` in STATUS.md format (`jrnb2024-pim** (open)`) and is absent in DISPATCH-NOTE prose format (`jrnb2024-pim (pending)`). With this change:
- Example 1 (`- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open): Renovate...`) correctly PASSES — regex finds slug, then `**`, then ` (open):`.
- Example 2 (`See TF-024X-conflict-jrnb2024-pim (pending): adopter...`) correctly PASSES — regex finds slug, no `**`, then ` (pending):`.
- Examples 3–6 correctly FAIL for the intended reason (no status field / empty description / whitespace description / short description) rather than failing due to `**`.

Update only the regex at line 52 in the plan-doc. The prose description at line 55 does not need to change (it describes file-agnosticism correctly). The §6 024B acceptance row references 'invariant 2's regex format spec literally' — once invariant 2's regex is corrected, 024B inherits the fix via cross-reference.

Also update the format spec block header at line 49 to add a closes marker: '+ 024A R7 R7-NEW-CRIT-001 (completeness — regex does not match STATUS.md bold format; worked Example 1 fails when it should pass)'.

findings.title: DISPATCH-NOTE acceptance criterion (iii) says 'three-path cascade-status' and DISPATCH-NOTE risk surface item 4 says 'three-path CI enforcement' — both stale after R6 added the fail-closed default as a fourth CI behavior
findings.evidence:
**DISPATCH-NOTE criterion (iii) (line 51):**
'operator-run + invocation-logged + CI-enforced (**three-path cascade-status**: `onboarded` / `onboarded-operator-bump` / `blocked-on-adopter-conflict`; positive evidence + meaningful-content regex match + negative assertion where applicable per invariant 2)'

**DISPATCH-NOTE risk surface item 4 (line 69):**
'D-035's CI-refusal + **invariant 2's three-path CI enforcement** (per `cascade-status:` field — `onboarded` and `onboarded-operator-bump` paths require log entry + target match; `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` path requires log file NOT modified + TF reference with meaningful content per regex spec)'

Fix-round-6 added an explicit fail-closed default as a FOURTH CI behavior to invariant 2: 'if `cascade-status:` is absent OR contains a value not in the enumerated set `{onboarded, onboarded-operator-bump, blocked-on-adopter-conflict}`, the script exits non-zero (CI fails).' This is structurally distinct from the three named check-paths (it activates when no valid cascade-status value is present, not when one of the three named values is present). §6 024B acceptance explicitly enumerates 'all four CI behaviours' and lists fail-closed as the first behavior.

Both DISPATCH-NOTE loci still describe the CI enforcement as 'three-path' — a label that was accurate before fix-round-6 but is now stale. A reviewer applying criterion (iii) as a completeness checklist would verify that invariant 2 covers three paths; they would NOT be prompted to verify the fail-closed default. The completeness criterion is therefore incomplete as an acceptance check for the post-R6 invariant 2.

Completeness governance classification: MAJ (not MIN) because the DISPATCH-NOTE acceptance criteria are the normative acceptance gate for this slice — criterion (iii) is what a slice reviewer checks against. A stale criterion (iii) that says 'three-path' may cause a reviewer to accept invariant 2 without verifying the fail-closed default, even though §6 024B now requires 'all four CI behaviours'. The inconsistency between criterion (iii) ('three-path') and §6 024B ('four CI behaviours') creates an acceptance-criterion coherence gap.
findings.recommendation:
Update DISPATCH-NOTE criterion (iii): replace 'three-path cascade-status: `onboarded` / `onboarded-operator-bump` / `blocked-on-adopter-conflict`' with 'four-behavior cascade-status enforcement: three named paths (`onboarded` / `onboarded-operator-bump` / `blocked-on-adopter-conflict`) + fail-closed default (absent or unrecognised value → CI exits non-zero) per invariant 2. (Closes 024A R6 R6-NEW-MAJ-003 safety — fail-closed added to DISPATCH-NOTE acceptance criterion.)'

Update DISPATCH-NOTE risk surface item 4: replace 'invariant 2's three-path CI enforcement' with 'invariant 2's four-behavior CI enforcement (three named cascade-status check-paths + fail-closed default for absent/unrecognised values)'.

Note: R5-NEW-MIN-001 closes at criterion (iii) was the update that added 'three-path cascade-status: onboarded / onboarded-operator-bump / blocked-on-adopter-conflict' — that update was correct for R5 but is now one step behind R6's fail-closed addition.

findings.title: §7 R-024-07 still says 'status field + non-empty description' — pre-R6 paraphrase; R6-NEW-MAJ-002 safety propagation gap; the \S non-whitespace anchor and ≥20-char minimum are both absent from this risk-row description
findings.evidence:
Plan-doc §7 R-024-07 mitigation (line 225) reads: 'the cascade slice MUST file a forward TF (`TF-024X-renovate-<adopter-slug>`) **as a STATUS.md "Tracked-forward items" row using exactly the standardised prefix `TF-024X-renovate-` followed by the adopter's `<owner>-<repo>` slug, with meaningful content** (status field + non-empty description after the slug — bare-prefix stubs fail the CI check per invariant 2; closes 024A R4 R4-NEW-MAJ-002 safety).'

The parenthetical paraphrase says 'status field + non-empty description after the slug'. This is the pre-fix-round-5 framing — the R4 MAJ-002 fix that introduced 'meaningful content' terminology. It omits:
1. The ≥20 character minimum (introduced at R5 via the regex spec)
